record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: For the axion potential induced by virtual dyonic loops, is the dilute approximation in which a single dyon loop dominates and long-range Coulomb interactions between dyons are ignored actually valid, and if so in what regime?

evidence.quote: Analogous to the dilute instanton approximation, the computations in Ref. [113] involving dyons assume that the effective axion potential is dominated by a single dyon loop and ignore the long-range Coulomb interactions between the dyons. The validity of the assumption needs to be checked.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a four-dimensional gauge theory containing an axion field $a$ coupled to an Abelian gauge field through the topological term $(a/8\pi^2) F\wedge F$, together with a heavy magnetic monopole of mass $M$ and 't Hooft–Polyakov type. By the Witten effect, a nonzero axion background shifts the electric charge of a monopole, making it a dyon, and Euclidean monopole worldlines that wind around the dyon collective coordinate generate an effective axion potential of the schematic form
$$V(a) \;\sim\; -K\,\cos(a) \,,$$
where the prefactor $K$ is computed from a single Euclidean dyon-loop configuration, in direct analogy with the dilute instanton gas approximation: one assumes (i) the path integral over dyon worldlines is dominated by a single isolated loop, and (ii) the long-range Coulomb interactions (both electric and magnetic) between dyons and anti-dyons can be neglected.

Question. Determine whether this dilute single-dyon-loop approximation for the axion potential is in fact valid in a controlled regime, and if so, identify explicitly the regime of parameters (e.g.\ monopole mass $M$, gauge coupling $g$, axion decay constant $f_a$, temperature, density of monopoles, and any infrared scale) in which the corrections from multi-loop configurations and from long-range Coulomb interactions between dyons are parametrically suppressed. In particular, give quantitative criteria on these parameters under which the single-loop result for $K$ provides the leading contribution to $V(a)$, or otherwise demonstrate that no such regime exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2021 PRL on "Axion Mass from Magnetic Monopole Loops" and a 2025 follow-up "Dyon Loops and Abelian Instantons") computes the axion potential from a single dilute dyon loop and discusses consistency checks (e.g. behavior in the presence of light fermions, robustness against higher-derivative corrections), but a systematic derivation of the regime of validity of the dilute approximation, including the neglect of long-range Coulomb interactions between dyons, does not appear to be established in the literature. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Axion Mass from Magnetic Monopole Loops
status_evidence.snippet: Axion potential generated by Euclidean monopole worldlines winding around the dyon collective coordinate, computed in a single-loop (dilute) approximation.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the single-dyon-loop computation whose validity regime is at issue.

status_evidence.title: Dyon Loops and Abelian Instantons
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Coulomb self-energy of regulated dyon loop configurations and consistency of the dyon-loop induced axion potential under various corrections.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work addresses some but not all aspects of the dilute approximation; full validity regime not pinned down.

status_evidence.title: Confining Dyon-Anti-Dyon Coulomb Liquid Model
status_evidence.snippet: Treats dense dyon-anti-dyon ensembles with long-range Coulomb interactions via Debye–Hückel-type corrections, indicating that Coulomb effects can be non-negligible beyond the strictly dilute limit.
status_evidence.claim: Shows that Coulomb interactions are important in non-dilute regimes, underscoring the need to delineate where the dilute approximation holds.
